questions.question: In the Common Crawl ecosystem, what is a WARC file primarily used for?
questions.choice_A: Storing raw HTTP request/response payloads and crawl metadata as a sequence of records
questions.choice_B: Providing extracted link graphs and metadata only, without payloads
questions.choice_C: Offering pre-tokenized plain text suitable for direct language modeling
questions.choice_D: Indexing URLs to byte offsets for random access to records

questions.question: If your goal is to build a language model corpus with HTML removed and boilerplate stripped, which Common Crawl derivative is most appropriate to start from?
questions.choice_A: WARC
questions.choice_B: WAT
questions.choice_C: WET
questions.choice_D: CDX

questions.question: Which technique is most appropriate for near-duplicate detection of web documents that may have minor edits or paraphrasing?
questions.choice_A: URL-based exact matching
questions.choice_B: MinHash over token shingles with locality-sensitive hashing
questions.choice_C: Exact bytewise hashing (e.g., SHA-256)
questions.choice_D: Title string equality

questions.question: Why is URL-based deduplication alone often insufficient for web-scale corpora?
questions.choice_A: Because URLs cannot be normalized across protocols
questions.choice_B: Because content never changes at a given URL
questions.choice_C: Because HTTP responses cannot be hashed reliably
questions.choice_D: Because the same content can appear at many distinct URLs (e.g., with tracking parameters, mirrors, or syndication)

questions.question: When grouping pages by site for analysis, what is a robust way to identify the registrable domain?
questions.choice_A: Use the Public Suffix List to extract the effective TLD+1 (e.g., example.co.uk)
questions.choice_B: Take the last two labels of the hostname blindly
questions.choice_C: Strip everything after the first dot in the hostname
questions.choice_D: Use the path’s first segment as the domain

questions.question: In an iterative data mining pipeline that expands from a seed corpus, what is a primary risk that must be actively mitigated?
questions.choice_A: Insufficient storage throughput for WARC files
questions.choice_B: Semantic drift, where the corpus gradually shifts away from the intended domain
questions.choice_C: Over-normalization of URLs
questions.choice_D: Excessive compression ratios in WET files

questions.question: To reduce benchmark contamination by n-gram matching between training data and held-out benchmarks, which configuration reduces false positives while retaining meaningful matches?
questions.choice_A: Short n (e.g., 3) with any match flagged
questions.choice_B: Short n with very low frequency thresholds
questions.choice_C: Long n with a zero-overlap policy
questions.choice_D: Longer n (e.g., 13–20) with a minimum number of overlapping n-grams or a high fraction overlap threshold

questions.question: For language identification on noisy, short web snippets, which practice improves reliability at the document level?
questions.choice_A: Relying solely on top-1 prediction from a character n-gram classifier
questions.choice_B: Inferring language from TLD or domain country code
questions.choice_C: Aggregating sentence-level predictions with confidence scores and applying a minimum-confidence threshold
questions.choice_D: Counting stopwords from a single language

questions.question: A multilingual site hosts mixed-language pages under the same domain. What is the best strategy for language labeling?
questions.choice_A: Perform per-document language identification with thresholds, allowing for mixed-language tags if needed
questions.choice_B: Assign the whole domain to one language based on homepage detection
questions.choice_C: Infer language solely from server IP geolocation
questions.choice_D: Ignore language and rely on downstream models to cope

questions.question: When building data quality filters for a web-scale corpus, what is a key pitfall to avoid when using a learned quality classifier?
questions.choice_A: Using any human labels for calibration
questions.choice_B: Overfitting the filter to proxy signals so it removes novel but valuable content; periodic blind audits help prevent this
questions.choice_C: Combining multiple weak signals into an ensemble
questions.choice_D: Logging feature importances for review

questions.question: Which statement best contrasts SimHash and MinHash for near-duplicate detection?
questions.choice_A: Both require exact string equality to match
questions.choice_B: SimHash estimates Jaccard similarity while MinHash uses cosine similarity
questions.choice_C: SimHash maps high-dimensional features to a binary fingerprint enabling Hamming-distance LSH; MinHash approximates Jaccard similarity via permutations of shingles
questions.choice_D: MinHash is only suitable for exact duplicates

questions.question: You plan to filter exact substrings of benchmark items from training data using fixed-length n-grams. What is a scalable approach to implement this at web scale?
questions.choice_A: Build a full-text inverted index for the entire corpus first
questions.choice_B: Serialize all substrings into a relational database
questions.choice_C: Use regex scans over raw HTML streams
questions.choice_D: Compute rolling hashes (e.g., Rabin–Karp) for n-grams and query a Bloom filter or hash set built from benchmark n-grams

questions.question: What is the most practical way to locate and fetch specific records from Common Crawl without downloading entire WARC files?
questions.choice_A: WAT files contain byte offsets for WARC records
questions.choice_B: Use the CDX index to map URLs to byte ranges and perform HTTP range requests against WARC files on S3/HTTPS
questions.choice_C: WET files include the original HTML payloads for random access
questions.choice_D: Common Crawl provides per-URL JSON APIs with full payloads for all snapshots

questions.question: To deduplicate pages that share templates but differ in navigation and ads, which approach is most effective?
questions.choice_A: Boilerplate removal followed by token shingling and Jaccard similarity with a tuned threshold
questions.choice_B: Comparing raw HTML byte-for-byte
questions.choice_C: Matching only the meta description tag
questions.choice_D: Blocking by domain and keeping only one page per domain

questions.question: Which domain-level heuristic is most reliable for flagging low-quality or spammy sites at scale?
questions.choice_A: High number of outbound links on the homepage
questions.choice_B: Use of a country-code TLD
questions.choice_C: A very high fraction of pages that are near-duplicates of each other across many URLs
questions.choice_D: Presence of analytics scripts

questions.question: How can you mitigate bias introduced by a seed corpus when iteratively expanding a web-scale dataset?
questions.choice_A: Only crawl from the top 100 domains by traffic
questions.choice_B: Freeze the seed set and never update it
questions.choice_C: Lower the quality thresholds to capture more diverse data
questions.choice_D: Diversify seeds across sources and languages, use active learning, and periodically re-seed with human-reviewed examples

questions.question: In designing a human-in-the-loop labeling process to improve data quality filters, what sampling strategy best balances efficiency and impact?
questions.choice_A: Uniform random sampling from the entire corpus
questions.choice_B: Stratified sampling emphasizing high-uncertainty items and covering diverse sources/domains
questions.choice_C: Sampling only items that the model scores as very high quality
questions.choice_D: Sampling only from previously seen domains

questions.question: What is a bandwidth-efficient method to retrieve only the needed parts of WARC files from Common Crawl?
questions.choice_A: Use byte-range HTTP requests guided by CDX offsets to stream just the target records
questions.choice_B: Download full WARC files and discard unneeded records locally
questions.choice_C: Request pre-split per-record files from Common Crawl
questions.choice_D: Convert WARC to WET first and then extract the desired records

questions.question: When setting the Jaccard similarity threshold for near-duplicate detection with shingles, how should you choose it to balance precision and recall?
questions.choice_A: Set it arbitrarily high to minimize any duplicates
questions.choice_B: Use the same threshold across all domains and content types
questions.choice_C: Perform a sweep on labeled examples, evaluate precision–recall trade-offs, and pick a threshold that meets contamination and coverage goals
questions.choice_D: Always use 0.5 because it balances matches by definition

questions.question: Beyond exact or n-gram substring filtering, which additional practice reduces benchmark contamination risk in training data?
questions.choice_A: Increasing the learning rate during training
questions.choice_B: Removing all content from the same top-level domain as the benchmark host
questions.choice_C: Using smaller batch sizes
questions.choice_D: Time- or domain-based splits (e.g., exclude documents newer than the benchmark release date and from benchmark-related domains)
